title: Verification abundance, adjudication scarcity: what happens to mathematical knowledge when proof checking becomes free
abstract: arXiv:2608.28997v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In May 2026 an OpenAI model produced a counterexample to the Erd\H{o}s unit distance conjecture. Five mathematicians published a human-verified version the same day, and the result entered the literature within weeks. In August 2026 the same laboratory published ten mathematical and theoretical computer science results, each accompanied by a machine-checkable Lean 4 certificate with no unproved steps. Four weeks later, one remained the subject of an unresolved dispute over whether its formalization meant what it claimed.   We argue that this difference is structural. We distinguish three layers of verification: derivational validity, which a kernel checks; representational fidelity, whether the formal statement means the intended question; and epistemic significance. translated_title: 验证过剩，裁决稀缺：当证明检验变得免费时，数学知识将何去何从
translated_abstract: 2026年5月，一个OpenAI模型给出了埃尔德什单位距离猜想的反例。五位数学家在同一天发表了经人工验证的版本，该结果在数周内进入了文献。2026年8月，同一实验室发表了十项数学与理论计算机科学成果，每项成果都附带一份机器可检验、不含未证步骤的Lean 4证书。然而四周之后，其中一项成果仍陷于一场未决的争议：其形式化究竟是否表达了它所声称的含义。我们认为这种差异是结构性的。我们区分了验证的三个层次：推导有效性，可由内核检验；表征保真度，即形式化陈述是否表达了原本想问的问题；以及认识论意义。只有第一层是可以机械化的。因此，使证明检验变得近乎免费并不会消除验证工作，而是将负担转移到了依赖于稀缺专家注意力的层次上。
tldr: 论文提出，当证明检验被机械化而变得近乎免费时，验证工作并不会消失，而是转移到机器无法处理的表征保真度与认识论意义层次，使得依赖稀缺专家注意力的“裁决”成为数学知识生产的新瓶颈。
en_tdlr: When machine proof checking becomes free, verification work does not vanish but structurally shifts to the non-mechanizable layers of representational fidelity and epistemic significance, making scarce expert adjudication the new bottleneck for mathematical knowledge.
